samples.question: This picture contains one small block drawn with a thick black frame; every pale grey mark outside that frame is inert decoration that changes nothing. Inside the frame is a grid of nine square cells in three rows and three columns, and beneath the grid a strip holding small green squares. Each cell holds zero, one, two or three red dots. Exactly one cell is outlined by a blue square: that is the drop cell. The number of green squares in the bottom strip is the number of grains dropped, one at a time, onto the drop cell, and each grain adds one red dot to it. Whenever a cell holds four or more dots it topples: it loses four dots and sends one dot to each of the cells immediately above, below, left and right of it, and any dot sent past the edge of the grid is discarded. Toppling continues until no cell holds four or more dots, and the stable result does not depend on the order in which the topples are carried out. How many red dots are in the drop cell once no cell can topple any more? Answer 0, 1, 2 or 3.
